nodes.title: Charter and acceptance baseline
nodes.summary: Freeze the build charter: fixed context D01-D03 and founder decision D04 (every user type manages API tokens so its own agents can carry out every account action under the same gates), P1/P2/P3 vocabulary, Q12 option 1 as a reversible decision with its swap points (custody Fireblocks-type, bank Monoova/Zepto-type, registry IQ-EQ/Automic-type, identity Equifax/Sumsub/Averer-type), the human gates list (HG-LEGAL, HG-VENDOR/ACCOUNTS, HG-KEYS, HG-AUDIT, HG-PENTEST, HG-CAPITAL, HG-PROD, HG-REVIEW, HG-LAUNCH), the canonical screen table reconciling design codes to product-map codes (design INV-01 = POR-01, INV-02 = INV-01+INV-02, INV-03 = POR-04) and renumbering the five undrawn admin screens to ADM-36 sign-in and 2FA, ADM-37 users/roles/access reviews, ADM-38 investor directory, ADM-39 entities register and detail, ADM-40 token registry list so they never clash with ADM-35, and the coverage matrix mapping every one of the 91 screens, 21 journeys, 22 gates, 27 modules and 14 state machines to a node or an exclusion. Records the SHA-256 of the design folder, never edited. D04 frozen as data: (a) the non-delegable action list (identity and liveness, first passkey and wallet, creating or widening tokens, changing the withdrawal account, recovery and guardian changes, closing the account) that no scope can cover; (b) HG-LEGAL counsel questions as parameters: which declarations must be personal (wholesale status, target market), whether an agent may acknowledge disclosures under standing consent, whether a mandate changes the licence perimeter (G21), whether a sponsor agent counts as one of the sponsor's two people; (c) partner user types (trustee/RE, valuer, property manager, auditor, regulator observer, licensee) as principal type PARTNER with their surfaces; (d) the API contract: versioned REST with OpenAPI, MCP, webhooks, SDK, per-user sandbox, idempotency, rate limits, cursor pagination. Documentation only; pass criterion: the matrix has no gaps and no node edits another node's paths.

nodes.title: Domain ids, money and unit math
nodes.summary: Pure TypeScript: branded ids (APR-, OP-, RX-ORD-, INV-, AML-, TOK- for API tokens, MND- for mandates), integer-cent money with en-AU formatting, whole units, basis points, rounding rules (distribution lines round down, remainder to a rounding account, never lost), fee math (0.5% transaction fee, subtotal + fee = total to the cent), holder-cap arithmetic (qty/10,000 vs cap), price band (valuation x 85-115%), token valuation ((value + cash - debt - liabilities) / units), withholding rates as parameters (47% no-TFN, MIT 15%/30%), and screens.ts generated from the charter's canonical screen table. Property tests with fast-check are the oracle scope.

nodes.title: State machines, gate codes, approval codes and permission matrix as data
nodes.summary: All 14 state machines SM-00..SM-13 as transition tables with guards (every state and trigger from the catalogue), a generic engine that refuses any transition not in the table, gate codes G01-G22 with phase (G22 'Agent authority' applies to every agent-initiated action in every phase), approval policy codes (4E, 4E+Q, 6E, 6E+Q, SGL+R, AUTO), the 51-role list incl. AGNT and SVCA, the role x module x action matrix from which both RBAC and API-token scopes are derived (a scope is a matrix cell, so a token can never name a right its owner lacks; every cell carries a delegable flag and the charter's non-delegable actions are flagged false so no scope can include them; the matrix also has rows for the PARTNER principal types TP-RE, TP-VAL, TP-PM, TP-AUD, TP-OBS, TP-LIC), and the ten SoD rules as data incl. 'an agent is never a checker or a custody signer'. Exhaustive transition tests and forbidden-transition tests are the oracle scope.

nodes.title: Database schema, migrations and row-level security
nodes.summary: Drizzle schema for every entity in the architecture brief §3 (domains A-E) plus ApiToken, AgentPrincipal, AgentMandate and Alert, tenant_id on every row, _enc PII fields with envelope keys from the kms adapter interface, bitemporal RegisterEntry, integer cents, enum columns taken from the state machines, approval_id on privileged rows, on_behalf_of on audit rows, RLS policies per tenant, the insert-only trigger on audit_event, and migrations as reviewable files. RLS is tested by opening two tenant sessions.

nodes.title: Sandbox adapter framework, config and phase flags
nodes.summary: packages/adapters/core: the adapter registry selected by ADAPTER_<NAME>=sandbox|vendor, the conformance-suite harness every adapter must pass, magic-input scenario conventions, health reporting for ADM-32, and the sandbox operator hooks. packages/config: zod env schema, RUN_MODE=local refusing any production adapter, phase flags P1/P2/P3 defaults (offers.wholesale on; offers.retail, resale.board, payouts.stablecoin, platform.inflow_freeze off; agents.traffic on). A test asserts no production selector exists in the build. Documents every Q12 swap point. Also the kms/secrets adapter (getSecret, encrypt, decrypt, sign; sandbox = local encrypted store with a dev master key used by A04 envelope keys and the A15 keystore; swap: cloud KMS/HSM under HG-KEYS) and the storage adapter (putObject, getObject, presignUpload; sandbox = docker volume, sha256-addressed, encrypted, size and type limits) for every uploaded document and generated PDF; swap: any S3-compatible store.

nodes.title: API and worker skeleton with OpenAPI-generated SDK
nodes.summary: Fastify 5 with zod type providers, OpenAPI generated from route schemas into packages/sdk (typed client), request, approval and on_behalf_of ids on every log line (pino with schema-driven redaction), OpenTelemetry hooks, health endpoints, idempotency keys on writes, per-principal rate-limit hook, module registration with the boundary lint, and the pg-boss worker process with the transactional outbox. Rule for every later service node: read contracts (list, detail and read-model schemas) are published into the OpenAPI document in the node's first commit so packages/sdk types and the MCP tool catalogue exist before the engine passes. Both processes run in compose against Postgres. Cursor pagination on every list endpoint, the /v1 prefix and deprecation-header hook (policy in A99), and an injectable clock as the only source of 'now': in RUN_MODE=local a test endpoint advances it so timelocks, SLA clocks and expiries run in minutes, driving sandbox delays and Hardhat time too.

nodes.title: Append-only hash-chained audit log
nodes.summary: AuditEvent writes with prev_event_sha256 and event_sha256 over the canonical event, before/after hashes never PII copies, actor plus on_behalf_of (the human principal an agent or token acted for) on every event, the daily verification job (R18) writing the head hash to evidence, audited exports and unmask events, 7-year retention with legal holds. Oracle: any UPDATE or DELETE is refused at the database; a mutated row breaks verification; every privileged step later in the system leaves exactly one event; an event written under a token always carries on_behalf_of.

nodes.title: Authentication, sessions, RBAC and segregation of duties
nodes.summary: WebAuthn passkeys for investors and sponsor users (resident credentials, login passkeys separate from wallet passkeys), staff passkeys with hardware attestation required, server-side sessions with device binding and idle timeouts, 30-day dormancy lock, tenant context per request, 'view as tenant' audited, RBAC middleware generated from the permission matrix, the ten SoD rules enforced at role grant and at request time, break-glass sessions (2-of-3, at most 4 h, recorded), a principal model with types HUMAN, PARTNER (trustee/RE, valuer, property manager, auditor, regulator observer, licensee; the rows and portal are A98), AGNT and SVCA where AGNT is maker-only and can never hold a checker or signer role, and a 'fresh assertion' primitive (a WebAuthn assertion no older than N minutes over a given payload hash) that later nodes use for token creation, scope widening and passkey-confirmed actions. Oracle: generated tests for every matrix cell; no self-grant; SUPER never holds a money or signer role. Also email verification at sign-up and lost-login-passkey recovery (magic link, re-verification, cooling period, sessions revoked), separate from wallet recovery SM-13.
design_refs: design:bug 16 login placeholder replaced by passkey sign-in

nodes.title: API tokens, scopes, agent principals and mandates for every user type (G22)
nodes.summary: Founder decision D04 as a core auth capability every later API route inherits. ApiToken per principal of every user type: personal tokens for investors, tenant-scoped tokens for sponsor users (issued under SP-OWN approval), staff tokens (only after a hardware-key assertion), partner tokens for PARTNER principals (A98); scopes generated from the role x module x action matrix so a token can never exceed its owner's rights and can never include a non-delegable action (the G22 evaluator refuses those regardless of scope). Token secrets shown once, stored only as a hash with a type prefix (rx_inv_, rx_spn_, rx_ptr_, rx_stf_, rx_sb_ sandbox), one named agent per token, per-token limits (per-action and daily amount caps in cents, allowed vehicles and properties, allowed actions, time windows, expiry, optional IP allow-list, rate limits), rotation, last-used tracking, immediate revoke that fails closed within one request (cache invalidated synchronously). AgentPrincipal (AGNT) and AgentMandate rows binding a token to a named human (on_behalf_of), a scope set, spending and quantity caps, expiry and revocation; creation and widening need a fresh passkey assertion by the human. Token-bound confirmation: actions the design confirms with a passkey (order confirm, withdrawal request) may be pre-authorised within a mandate's caps through a mandate signing key registered under that assertion, so an agent can complete every account action within its mandate while every money-moving action still passes the ordinary gates and maker-checker; above the caps the human's passkey is required. Joint accounts follow their signing rule; entity accounts issue tokens only through a verified signatory. G22 'Agent authority' evaluator as a pure function in packages/domain (mandate live, scope covers module and action, limits hold, the human still holds the role, the agent is never the checker for a request its principal or a sibling agent made and never a custody signer), the middleware running it on every token call and recording a GateEvaluation naming the missing scope, the platform-wide agents.traffic kill switch (SGL+R once the approvals engine exists; a flag until then; per-user and per-tenant tiers are A101), and the token-introspection interface that A104, A99 and A101 consume. Oracle (hidden): a token cannot act outside its owner's cell; a revoked token or mandate fails within one request; an agent can never be a checker; a G22 refusal names the missing scope; widening without a fresh assertion is refused; a non-delegable action is refused even when a scope names it; every agent-written audit event carries on_behalf_of; a token secret never appears in a log, audit event or column.

nodes.title: Alerts and SLA-clocks service
nodes.summary: Alert model for the 17 alert types of the catalogue with severities Sev1 (15 min), Sev2 (1 h), Sev3 (1 business day), Sev4, business-day clocks in AEST/AEDT incl. public holidays as data, owners by role, acknowledge / assign / escalate / snooze with a mandatory reason, bulk acknowledge for Sev3/4 only, the 07:00 daily digest job, a queue-SLA-breach detector, and typed emission hooks that reconciliation, identity, treasury, property, wallets, AML, licences, approvals (SGL+R ratification timers) agent-access (revocation storms, kill switch) and the agent guard (anomaly holds) call. Backend for ADM-02 and the ADM-01 tiles.

nodes.title: Approvals engine and maker-checker (SM-00)
nodes.summary: ApprovalRequest with APR-<yyyymmdd>-<base32> ids, canonical payload and payload_sha256, ApprovalPolicy rows as versioned data (thresholds, checker role sets, TTL 72 h, timelocks 48/72 h), precheck hook interface for the rules engine, SoD exclusion of the maker through every route (direct, delegation, agent or token acting on behalf of the maker, mid-flight role change), WebAuthn assertion over the payload hash stored per decision (never satisfiable by a token), SGL+R act-first with a 2 h ratification timer that raises Sev2 through the alerts service and auto-reverts where reversible, AUTO only on an exact hash match, expiry and cancellation, bulk approve for low-risk types only. Agents and tokens may submit requests (maker) and never approve them. Oracle §6.3 of the architecture brief plus: a checker decision presented with a token credential is refused.

nodes.title: Custody sandbox adapter and policy engine P1-P10
nodes.summary: CustodyAccount records V1 owner 3-of-5 (48-72 h timelock), V2 token agent 2-of-3, V3 pauser 1-of-N restrict-only, V4 identity agent auto within policy, V7 paymaster with daily cap and runway alert, V5/V6 reserved. Local encrypted keystore generated on first run (no value), EIP-712 attestation key, policy rules P1 approval-ID binding, P2 function allow-list, P3 supply guard, P4 destination guard, P5 amount bands, P6 time window, P9 initiator not signer (and never an AGNT principal), P10 timelock, and CustodyOp states prepared to reconciled. Signer approvals are console actions under each signer's own hardware-key login. Rotation schedule modelled. Swap point: Fireblocks-type engine behind the same adapter interface and conformance suite. Oracle: nothing signs without an approved request; a replayed approval id is refused; a signing request carrying a token credential is refused.

nodes.title: Client-money ledger (double entry)
nodes.summary: LedgerAccount and LedgerEntry: one AUD account per investor, escrow account per offering, trust bank mirror, fee and rounding accounts, operating account marked 'not client money' and never counted; every journal balanced in one transaction; available vs reserved balances; withdrawal thresholds as configuration (design default A$50k second approval, A$25k AUTO to an allow-listed account); ledger balance snapshots at a statement cut; read contracts for the wallet and activity screens published to the SDK. Oracle: property tests that no cent is created or destroyed across 100,000 random journal sequences; reserved never exceeds balance; operating excluded from client-money totals.

nodes.title: Bank rail sandbox adapter (NPP/PayID/PayTo) and receipt matching
nodes.summary: Bank adapter interface (createVirtualAccount per investor PayID, listTransactions, createPayout, createPayToMandate stub, statement feed, webhook) with a sandbox bank: virtual accounts, an API and console panel to 'receive' a payment with a payer name, random NPP delay scenarios, returned payments, duplicate webhooks, daily statements. Matching engine: payer name must match the verified investor or the receipt is held; manual match above A$10k routes to CFO; unmatched receipts older than 48 h alert; cash over A$10k flags a TTR line for AML. Swap point: Monoova/Zepto-type rail. Oracle: a mismatched name never credits a wallet; matching is idempotent under webhook retries.

nodes.title: Unit register (legal record) and registry sandbox adapter
nodes.summary: RegisterEntry (bitemporal, lots with acquired_at, price and lock_in_until), RegisterVersion certification (REGO then trustee, 4E), register instructions issue/transfer/redeem/adjust with acks, 'register first' rule (no mint reference without a register entry), cap table as-of date, signed extracts, logged exports, monthly certification, register adjustment as 6E (REGO to CCO + CFO plus trustee). Escrow balances are never register entries (design bug 14). Registry adapter sandbox applies instructions with configurable delay, produces the 02:00 CSV extract, can reject or drift for recon tests. Swap point: IQ-EQ/Automic-type registry or the trustee's own register. Oracle: an adjustment without 6E is refused; extracts reproduce entries exactly; export writes an audit event.

nodes.title: Rules engine: gates G01-G22, rule packs, threshold monitors, simulator
nodes.summary: GateEvaluation for every action (order, transfer, mint, distribution line, withdrawal, agent call) storing inputs hash, result, reason codes and rule_pack_version so decisions replay; RulePack AU-W-2026.1 (immutable once effective; AU-R-2027.1 as a P2 stub), per-token ComplianceRule parameters with params_sha256; FIRB eligibility matrix by property type (established residential residents-only until 30 Jun 2029, commercial and BTR after FIRB checks); ThresholdMonitor for holder cap 90%, landholder duty, foreign %, s601ED member count (default 20); simulator showing holders a change would breach; investor-specific overrides with legal basis and end date; every gate evaluator is a pure function with a fix-it message; G22 registered from the agent-authority package so every agent-initiated action is evaluated and replayable here like any other gate. Gates not yet backed by a service (G05, G09, G15) return 'not applicable in this phase'. Oracle: vectors per gate incl. a 500-token order failing G07 naming the maximum allowed and an agent order over its mandate cap failing G22 naming the cap.

nodes.title: Three-way reconciliation engine with zero tolerance
nodes.summary: Pure comparison functions in packages/domain/src/recon over snapshot objects (register version, chain snapshot, bank statement) implementing R1-R18 (R9, R15, R16 stubbed), ReconRun reproducible from its three keys, ReconBreak with type, delta, owner and proposed fix raised through the alerts service, targeted runs after every CustodyOp and registry ack, pre-flight runs before mint, distribution approval and (P2) board opening, the 02:00 AEST nightly job. While a Sev1 break is open for a vehicle: G10 halt flag set, mints, burns and payouts refused for it. Chain snapshot source is an interface with an in-memory stub here; the chain adapter node registers the real indexer source. Oracle: planted drifts (9,998 vs 10,000 units, unknown holder, bank delta of one cent) produce exactly the expected break set and halts; a break closes only on a clean re-run.

nodes.title: Licences, feature flags and licence perimeter (G21)
nodes.summary: Licence and CAR register with authorisations, conditions and expiry alerts T-90/30/7; FeatureFlag bound to a licence record with auto-revert when the binding lapses; toggles as 4E (SUPER to CCO) refused without a binding; DAF Act low-value exemption meter (A$10m trailing 12 months, A$5k per client, Sev2 at 80%); launch state resale/retail/stablecoins off; listing visibility mode configurable. Every phase-gated module reads flags from here. Kill switches and halts are owned by the halts node, which reads and sets the platform flags through this module's API.

nodes.title: Identity/DVS and sanctions sandbox adapters
nodes.summary: Identity adapter (startVerification, getResult, webhook, verifyEntity, resolveUbo) with scenarios keyed by name suffix (approve, refer, reject, PEP, fraud), simulated DVS two-source match and liveness score, ABN/ACN lookup fixtures. Sanctions adapter (screenPerson, screenEntity, screenWallet stub, subscribeListUpdates) shipping a fixture DFAT-style list with planted names and a list-update event. Conformance suites define what a real vendor must satisfy. Swap points: Equifax/Sumsub/Averer-type providers (HG-VENDOR).

nodes.title: Whole-stack Docker boot (AM1 exit)
nodes.summary: infra/stack compose profile for postgres, api, worker, hardhat (auto-mine under test control, deterministic accounts), the sandbox panels (bank, identity, registry, custody signer) and an OTel collector stub; one command boots, migrates, seeds, deploys the T-REX reference suite to the local chain and reports health; sandbox keys generated on first run; the MCP server starts against the API and lists its tools. Pass criterion (milestone AM1 exit): stack green three boots in a row on Windows 11 Docker Desktop, the audit chain verifies, a token-authenticated call to a seeded read endpoint succeeds and the same call with a revoked token fails, and a test asserts no live adapter or mainnet RPC is selectable. Surfaces toolchain drift (Node 24, Hardhat 2 vs 3, T-REX compile, Playwright in Docker) about forty nodes before the investor preview.

nodes.title: ERC-3643 suite and RealX compliance modules
nodes.summary: Shared IdentityRegistryStorage, TrustedIssuersRegistry, ClaimTopicsRegistry (KYC_VERIFIED, SANCTIONS_CLEAR, WHOLESALE_AU, RESIDENCY_FIRB, TMD_FIT), ClaimIssuer, ONCHAINID factory; per-trust Token (0 decimals, 10,000 units default), IdentityRegistry, ModularCompliance with CountryAllowModule, MaxBalanceModule (holder cap), RealX HolderCountModule, LockInModule (per-holder unlock set at mint), HaltModule (V3 flag distinct from pause), DocumentAnchor; factory deploy script per vehicle with CREATE2 addresses. Oracle: canTransfer vectors for every module; forced transfers blocked while paused; a wallet not in the registry cannot receive; module parameter hash matches the approved rule. Audit before mainnet is HG-AUDIT (open).

nodes.title: AgentGateway and owner multisig: approval IDs bound on-chain
nodes.summary: AgentGateway.execute(approvalId, target, data, signerSigs, attestation): EIP-712 attestation check, unused approvalId, target+selector allow-list per vault, distinct-signer quorum with the attested maker excluded, per-approval mint cap, Executed event; a second restrict-only instance for V3; RealXOwnerMultisig 3-of-5 with 48 h timelock and veto during the queue. About 200 lines of custom Solidity, invariant-tested. Oracle: replayed id refused; attestation for one calldata cannot execute another; mint total over the cap reverts; maker among signers reverts.

nodes.title: Passkey smart wallet, paymaster and guardian recovery contracts
nodes.summary: ERC-4337 v0.7 smart account with P-256 passkey owners (RIP-7212 precompile when present, Solidity verifier on Hardhat), SmartAccountFactory (CREATE2, salt = investor id hash), RecoveryModule with two guardians (RealX guardian under 2-of-3 control and the investor's second device), proposeOwner with a 48 h timelock, veto by the old passkey, execution requiring the RealX guardian, RealXPaymaster (VerifyingPaymaster) sponsoring only RealX targets within per-wallet daily caps. Oracle: recovery cannot execute inside 48 h; veto works; paymaster refuses non-RealX targets; account cannot be drained by the guardian alone. Also a SessionKeyModule (D04): the owner passkey registers a delegated session key limited to allow-listed contracts and selectors, an amount cap, an expiry and a nonce, revocable at once by the owner or the RealX guardian; it can never change owners, guardians or keys. Oracle adds: no call outside the allow-list, over the cap, after expiry or after revocation.

nodes.title: Chain adapter, deployment manifests and indexer
nodes.summary: viem transport behind the chain adapter (Hardhat now, Base Sepolia and mainnet later by URL and chain id), typed ABIs and deployment manifests per chain in packages/contracts, Token registry rows (SM-06 designed to configured), the indexer building Holding read models at block N and matching Executed(approvalId) events to CustodyOp, direct balanceOf/totalSupply/isFrozen cross-checks, the chain snapshot source registered with the recon engine, stuck-transaction (30 min) and indexer-lag (5 min) alerts through the alerts service.

nodes.title: Token operations service (mint, burn, freeze, pause, forced transfer, recovery)
nodes.summary: The lifecycle of §6.2 end to end for every V2/V3 function: approval to CustodyOp to policy engine to gateway call to indexer confirmation to registry instruction to targeted recon to closed. Deploy token 6E+Q via V1; mint only against a locked Allocation file (CFO, plus CCO + CEO when not from a file); burn 4E+Q; pause SGL+R ratified in 2 h; unpause 6E+Q; forced transfer 6E+Q with 48 h timelock waivable only by CCO + CEO with a court order; recoveryAddress; lock-up dates 4E+Q; upgrade 72 h. Milestone AM2 exit lives here: one mint bound to an approval id round-trips on the local chain and a replayed id is refused at every layer. Oracle: a confirmed transaction the register does not reflect opens a break, not a success; supply never exceeds the allocation; nothing broadcasts with fewer than 2 signatures.

nodes.title: Wallet service: smart-account factory, bundler sandbox, guardians and recovery requests
nodes.summary: Wallet rows (passkey_aa, external, vault, paymaster), account creation from the wallet passkey (counterfactual address first so onboarding never waits on a deployment), sandbox bundler submitting handleOps from a funded local EOA (real bundler behind the same adapter on testnet), paymaster policy signer and runway alert below 3 days, guardian set-up requiring re-verification and a waiting period, RecoveryRequest (SM-13) with 48 h timelock, cancel from any signed-in device, notices to old channels, smart-wallet recovery attempted before the token-level fallback, gas-sponsorship policy change ENGO to CFO. Wallet mechanism kept behind an interface (open DAP design point). Oracle: recovery refused before timelock without a CCO + CEO waiver record; new wallet must be identity-registered; old balance zero after fallback. Mandates needing on-chain acts (P2 asks and bids, claim acceptance, ballots) get a session key registered under the mandate's fresh assertion (A12) with the mandate's contracts, functions, amounts and expiry; revoking the mandate revokes the key in the same request; the owner key never reaches an agent.

nodes.title: Investor onboarding, KYC cases and KYB (SM-01)
nodes.summary: Investor and Account records, investor types (individual, joint with either/both signing rule, SMSF, company, trust), residency and FIRB flag captured at creation, KYCCase per verification event with provider decision, screening hits, risk points, 24 h SLA clock, RFI with 30-day expiry, fraud auto-reject, EDD as 6E (KYCA to MLRO + senior manager), PEP clearance KYCA to MLRO (4E, reason code mandatory, tighter than the design's one-click), true sanctions match freezes silently, BeneficialOwner cases for entities (owners at 25% or more; entity cannot invest until every person is verified), periodic refresh, suspension. Masked PII by default with reason-coded unmask. Every endpoint callable under a scoped token.

nodes.title: On-chain identity and claims service (V4 identity agent)
nodes.summary: registerIdentity, updateCountry, deleteIdentity and claim issuance through the V4 auto-signing policy, only for KYCCase rows in state approved (the case model is owned by the onboarding node); IdentityClaim off-chain mirror with topic, validity and revocation; wholesale claim with a two-year expiry; residency/FIRB claim; the nightly sweep revoking expired claims; R4/R5 checks feeding recon; revoke as 4E; residency change as 4E with re-evaluation. Oracle: isVerified true only after an approved case; expired wholesale claim blocks a new wholesale purchase but not holding or selling; a deleted identity cannot receive.
design_refs: design:onb ONB-08 'linked to your verified identity'

nodes.title: Classification: wholesale certificates and target-market hooks (SM-02)
nodes.summary: InvestorClassification with basis (A$500k-in-this-offer per offer with CCO check, accountant's certificate valid two years from certificate date, sophisticated, professional), CLSR review queue, expiring at 30 days with reminders at 60 and 30, expiry lapsing the on-chain claim while holdings stay, renewal creating a new case without removing the valid claim, rejection and revocation. TMD questionnaire model and G05 evaluation hook stubbed behind offers.retail for the P2 scheme node.

nodes.title: Sponsor tenancy, entities, licences of sponsors and admission pipeline
nodes.summary: Tenant (sponsor) with guardrails a tenant cannot switch off (KYC required locked on, eligibility packs, holder-cap ceiling, fee caps), TenantUser roles SP-OWN/OPS/FIN/IR with 2FA, internal approval rules that cannot weaken platform minimums (a user never approves their own submission; a sponsor agent never approves anything), admission pipeline applied to KYB to background to fee agreement to approved to tenant created (KYCA to CCO 4E, PART to CCO 4E), Entity and Vehicle (Trust now, SubFund in P2) records, sponsor billing (listing fee, per-investor monthly fee, invoices; unpaid 30+ days pauses new listings), sponsor performance metrics and watchlist, suspension SGL+R (also revokes the tenant's tokens), revenue share.

nodes.title: Properties, valuations and proof of property (SM-03)
nodes.summary: Property master data with lifecycle SM-03 (title verification mandatory before spv_formed; owner of record custodian or trustee), due-diligence pack with missing or expired items blocking submission, Valuation records (panel valuer, at most 6 months old, listing valuation at most 3 months old, moves above 10% need comparable sales, committee publish 6E updating token valuation and the band reference), PropertyAttestation monthly with evidence and public flags as a flag separate from distribution approval (design bug 2; overdue 10 days pauses the sponsor's new offers), obligations calendar (rates, land tax, insurance), distress signals and legal hold as data consumed by the halts node, investment-committee approval 6E, rent-roll CSV import and valuer upload adapters.
design_refs: design:bug 2 attestation flag separate from distribution

nodes.title: Documents, disclosure library, e-sign and acknowledgements (G12)
nodes.summary: Versioned Document library (FSG, terms, privacy, complaints policy, fees; per-listing IM or PDS/SPDS, TMD, deed, valuation, notices) with sha256, effective dates, superseded kept and marked, 7-year retention and legal holds, publish as 4E (LEGL to CCO) with optional on-chain anchor via DocumentAnchor, acknowledgement records (document id, version, timestamp per order; documents must have been opened, and an agent acknowledging under a mandate is recorded as such with on_behalf_of and only when the holder has a standing-consent record created with a passkey and the counsel parameter in A00 allows delegated acknowledgement; otherwise the order waits for the person), cooling-off statement text per regime (wholesale none; retail per PDS, configurable), e-sign adapter sandbox (auto-sign after delay or console button), templates with sponsor placeholders, investor document vault. Also the deterministic PDF renderer for confirmations, advices, statements, extracts and board packs (same inputs, same bytes, sha256 recorded, stored through the storage adapter).

nodes.title: Offerings: offer terms, listing review, raise monitor (SM-04)
nodes.summary: Offering with regime, unit price, soft and hard caps, min and max ticket, per-investor cap 5% default, lock-in 3 months default per listing, close date, allocation rule (first-come or pro-rata), residency rule from property type, distribution policy and reserve months, sponsor retained stake, terms outside RealX limits needing a reason; rules simulation on save; submission draft to compliance_review (operator submits, owner approves, then RealX); listing review with pack constraints read-only, blockers and warnings, due-diligence sign-offs, 'return with comments'; go-live 4E+Q requiring the platform CCO; extend or material change 4E with investor re-confirmation within 5 business days; pause SGL+R; live raise funnel and escrow balance; not public until approved (design bug 19). Public and sponsor read contracts (listings by status, open offers, raise bars) published to the SDK first.

nodes.title: Orders, escrow, allocation and refunds (SM-05)
nodes.summary: Order lifecycle: submitted to eligibility_check (G01, G04, G06, G07 live and again at mint; G22 when placed under a token) to awaiting_funds (wholesale never enters reflection_period) to funded on payment match to allocated to settled only when both a register entry and a token delivery exist; cancel until close if the listing permits; the confirm step accepts either a fresh passkey assertion or a mandate signing key within the mandate's caps; escrow accounts per offering with Δ 0 against funded orders before any allocation; allocation workbench (first-come or pro-rata, scaled to hard cap, capped at 5% never silently accepted, ineligible at mint excluded and refunded) producing a locked Allocation file with sha256; refunds 4E within 5 business days; expiry of unfunded orders; confirmation records. Oracle: sum of allocations equals the file; sum of refunds equals funded orders on a failed raise; fee to the cent; G07 with existing holdings; an agent order above its mandate cap is refused by G22 and never reserves funds.
design_refs: design:buy stepper order lines and timeline

nodes.title: Finalise-and-mint and revert-and-refund pipelines
nodes.summary: Service-level J04 steps 7-13 and J05: close at end date or hard cap; soft cap reached or missed; finalising locks the allocation; escrow release 6E (FINA to CFO + CCO); trustee register entries first; batchMint per the locked file through the token operations service (6E+Q, V2 2-of-3); reconcile supply = register = allocations; order settled and confirmation issued; revert-and-refund 4E+Q with every order ending refunded and no tokens minted. Oracle: no mint before a register entry; supply not equal to register freezes the mint queue (Sev1); an ineligible recipient is excluded and refunded; the whole pipeline is idempotent under retries.

nodes.title: Treasury: withdrawals, escrow release, client-money reconciliation
nodes.summary: Withdrawal to the verified account only (name match, else held), sanctions re-screen and AML pattern check before every payout, AUTO up to the allow-listed threshold, TRSY to CFO 4E above it (default A$50k, configuration), a withdrawal request under a mandate is accepted within the mandate's amount band and refused above it by G22, AML restriction holds payouts and shows 'under review' to support, return of unmatched funds and internal transfers with dual bank authorisation, daily bank-vs-ledger reconciliation R10 with Δ 0 as a precondition for allocation, escrow release and distribution approval, payout-funding-short alert (7 days), fees and float-interest disclosure data.
design_refs: design:wallet Withdraw card and A$50k note

nodes.title: Distributions engine (SM-08)
nodes.summary: IncomePeriod from rent roll and expenses (gross rent - PM fee - maintenance and insurance - reserve top-up - management fee = net), record-date snapshot locked from a RegisterVersion before calculation, per-token amount and per-line gross with rounding down and remainder to the rounding account, variance checks vs last month and forecast, exceptions (AML hold with no notice, closed accounts, dust carried forward), approval chain sponsor accountant to sponsor owner to FINA to CFO (CEO above A$1m or 25% variance) bound to the payment file hash, funding (Δ 0 required), execution to AUD wallets, retries up to the approved amount then manual 4E, closed only when paid equals approved, zero or reduced declaration 6E, legal hold pauses, exit waterfall computation for the halts node. Oracle: changing a line after approval invalidates it; per-token x units at record date equals gross per line; R8 and R13 reproduce the file hash.

nodes.title: Tax engine: profiles, withholding, AMMA and CRS/FATCA
nodes.summary: TaxProfile (TFN/ABN encrypted, residencies and TINs, FATCA/CRS self-certification, consequence of no TFN explained), withholding engine applied per distribution line (no TFN 47%; MIT 15% or 30% for foreign residents; rates as versioned parameters), TaxComponent per run, AMMA statements per trust per year by 30 September, annual statements, cost base and lots, remittance and filing calendar, withholding rule edits 6E (TAXO to CCO + CFO). Oracle: withholding vectors to the cent; AMMA components sum to the year's lines; a TFN added mid-year changes only later lines.

nodes.title: AML screening, monitoring, cases and SMR clocks (SM-11)
nodes.summary: Screening hub (names and wallets, nightly re-screen at 03:00, re-screen before every payout, list-update hits Sev1), monitoring scenarios (rapid in/out, third-party deposits, round-tripping, unusual SMSF contribution, unusual agent-driven order bursts), alert to triage to case with need-to-know ACL limited to MLRO and CCO, restriction as freeze-now-ratify-later (CCO within 2 h, auto-escalates through the alerts service), wallet freeze creating a token operation, SMR clocks in business days (3, or 24 h for terrorism financing) with late filing surfaced as Sev1, TTR and IFTI items, RFI only after a tipping-off check, exit relationship MLRO to CCO. Oracle: SUPP and IRCM cannot read case fields through any API or token scope; investor-facing endpoints return no case data; clocks computed correctly across weekends and AEST/AEDT.

nodes.title: Communications, notifications, tasks and marketing claims (G17)
nodes.summary: Notification model by type and channel with preferences and 'mark all read', email and SMS sandbox adapters capturing into a local inbox used by e2e, templates, the worker jobs that turn events into the design's sponsor 'Needs you' tasks (from due dates: distribution approval, attestation due, RealX review changes) and investor notifications (offer opening and closing, income paid, certificate expiring, proof flags, and the agent notices A101 emits: a new token created or widened, first use from a new IP, every money-moving agent action above the person's notice threshold, anomaly holds and kill-switch events; plus daily agent activity summaries), sponsor announcements and significant-event notices with the RG 234 claims lint (configurable versioned blocked phrases such as 'guaranteed', 'capital protected', 'backed by real estate', 'beats the market'; yields need basis and date; treated as adversarial input), approval workflow IRCM to CCO (+ LEGL for material items), terms versions with 30-day notice, public KPIs 6E. Nothing publishes without an approval record.

nodes.title: Support, complaints (SM-12) and Investor 360 read model
nodes.summary: Tickets and the complaints register with acknowledgement and final-response clocks as parameters (defaults 5 and 30 days, marked 'set with counsel'), any dissatisfied ticket converts to a complaint, redress CMPH to CCO (+ CFO above A$5k), AFCA escalation with AFCA details shown, reopen and retention; Investor 360 aggregate (profile, limits, wallets, holdings, orders, payouts, tax, documents, cases, messages, votes, tokens and mandates, audit) masked by default with reason-coded unmask, support seeing only 'account under review'. Support cannot change money or records.

nodes.title: Reporting, regulatory calendar, filings and metric governance
nodes.summary: RegulatoryObligation calendar (AUSTRAC, ASIC, ATO, DDO, CAR obligations at 7/30/90 days) with owners and evidence, filing workspace (SMR, TTR, IFTI, CRS/FATCA, outside-TMD report stub with a 10-business-day clock), overdue filing Sev2, regulator and auditor data room with time-boxed scoped access (CCO to SECO), board and investor report exports (audited), metrics dictionary where 'capital raised' is defined and versioned and 'tokenised value' is never rendered, sponsor track-record figures for the public profile.

nodes.title: Job scheduler, integrations health and webhooks
nodes.summary: Cron schedules (snapshot 00:00, reconciliation 02:00, sanctions re-screen 03:00, claim expiry sweep, certificate reminders, attestation reminders, payout execution; the 07:00 digest is emitted by the alerts service) as idempotent replayable jobs, Job run history, Integration rows with health, latency and environment (sandbox or live) per adapter, WebhookSubscription with signed payloads and replay windows for sponsors and investors (subscriptions are scoped like tokens), RPC or network config change ENGO to SECO. Backend for ADM-32; tokens and mandates live in the agent-access module. Webhook subscriptions carry their creating token's scopes and stop when it is revoked; failed jobs land in a dead-letter list on ADM-32 with idempotent replay and a Sev3 alert.

nodes.summary: Read models for the investor and sponsor views: portfolio value at valuation and at last price equal to the sum of holdings, cash available and reserved, monthly income series, holding detail with average cost, income received, lock-in end, on-chain balance and register match date from the last reconciliation ('we are checking this with the trustee' on mismatch), transactions ledger with on-chain reference and confirmation PDF generation, distribution history per trust, sponsor register view (holders, class, residency, largest vs cap, last reconciliation, break banner, logged export), public transparency table per trust. All exposed as read scopes for tokens. Rows carry actor and on_behalf_of so activity shows 'placed by your agent <name>' where a mandate acted.

nodes.title: Halts, kill switches and wind-down
nodes.summary: Single owner of J21 and the emergency controls: Halt records per vehicle with cause (manual, meeting, valuation stale, recon break, token pause, distress) where published reopening criteria and an end date are mandatory (a halt without them is refused), ratification timers (halt 2 h, kill switch 2 h, board 24 h in P2) with auto-escalation through the alerts service, kill switches as SGL+R (global inflow freeze, marketplace suspend, all agent traffic) acting at once by setting the platform flags in the perimeter module, distressed and legal-hold transitions of SM-03 that pause distributions and new offers, exit approval, sale completion, exit waterfall hand-off to the distributions engine, burn request (burn = supply) and register close through token operations, 7-year retention flag on every trust record, runbooks R1-R9 as data. G10 reads the halt state from here. The agent-traffic switch here is the platform-wide tier; per-user and per-tenant tiers are A101 and call the same interface.

nodes.title: Money-path smoke through the SDK (AM3 exit and founder checkpoint)
nodes.summary: A 'money' compose profile and a Vitest suite over packages/sdk (no UI yet): onboard a seeded investor to approved with claims issued, pay in through the sandbox bank panel, place an order under a passkey and a second one under an agent mandate, close, allocate, register entry, mint on the local chain, targeted reconciliation, distribution run to paid with withholding, withdrawal above and below the threshold, a planted registry drift that halts the mint queue and clears on a clean re-run. nodes.title: Agent guard: anomaly detection, sensitive-action notices and tiered kill switches

Sensitive-action notices: a NoticePolicy per person (token created or widened, first use from a new IP, money-moving action above a threshold, mandate near its daily cap, anomaly hold, kill switch) delivered through A43 to the person's channels, never to the agent. Kill switches as tiers: per token (A12), per user ('pause all my agents', by the person with a passkey or staff with a reason), per tenant (SP-OWN or staff; also fired by tenant suspension), platform-wide (A48, SGL+R), each stopping exactly its tier within one request. Retention as one policy table: seven years for audit events, documents, register versions, approvals, distributions and tax records; legal holds override; an erasure request (Privacy Act) pseudonymises the investor, revokes tokens and mandates and seals the wallet-to-person link while chain data and the hash chain stay intact; a retention job refuses deletes inside the window and logs the attempt; regulator and auditor exports stripped of PII beyond the request. Tests: restore reproduces the hashes; erasure leaves the chain verifiable and the investor unfindable by name; an in-window delete is refused and audited.

Plus the key-rotation drill in the custody sandbox, the break-glass drill (2-of-3, 4 h expiry, review task) and the agent kill-switch drill across all tiers. Findings become fix items; the testnet re-run of R1 and R3 is recorded in A86's pack.
